from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r = PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:', len(r.pages))
text=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages,1):
    text.append(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n\\n'+p.extract_text())
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(text))
print(''.join(text[:3]))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('tmp/pdfs')
for pattern in ['page-*.png', 'paper-*.png']:
    for f in p.glob(pattern):
        f.unlink()
(p/'manuscript.txt').unlink()
print('Removed temporary PDF extracts and renders.')
PY"

strengths: The mean-point correspondence is an original, elegant way to generate useful hypotheses for the difficult four-point, three-view pose problem using established five-point and P3P solvers. The contribution is practically relevant, and the manuscript clearly acknowledges its approximate nature.

The empirical support is substantial: 90,000 triplets across 18 scenes and three datasets, two RANSAC frameworks, synthetic geometry/noise experiments, and ablations of refinement, filtering, perturbations, and thresholds. Supplementary evaluation using the maximum error across all three camera pairs strengthens confidence that the gains are not artifacts of the main metric.

Table 2 demonstrates useful improvements against a strong, equivalently augmented baseline. On PhotoTourism, 4p3v(A)+R+F+ENM achieves AUC@10 of 76.56 at 32.37 ms, compared with 76.20 at 56.52 ms for 5pt+P3P+R+F+ENM. The mean-point variants offer higher peak accuracy and greater robustness to threshold choices.

The explanation connects the approximation to its practical RANSAC integration clearly. Established solver components, a source-code link, documented hardware and parameters, and a separate validation scene provide good reproducibility support. Together with the extensive experiments, these merits support weak acceptance.
weaknesses: The runtime comparison with HC has a consequential initialization confound. Section 8.3, footnote 8 reports loading network weights/data once per RANSAC, taking approximately 45 ms, while Table 2 reports total HC times of approximately 60–67 ms. Such initialization could be amortized across repeated estimations. Table 4 appropriately excludes loading from standalone solver timings, but an equivalent end-to-end comparison with initialization amortized is missing; the claimed speed advantage over HC is therefore less convincing than the accuracy advantage.

The claim of a consistently best speed–accuracy trade-off is stronger than the comparison establishes. Figure 4 omits the 5pt+P3P+R+F variants that Table 2 shows are stronger baselines. Against the fully augmented baseline on PhotoTourism, the best-accuracy mean-point variant improves AUC@10 from 76.20 to 77.14 while increasing runtime from 56.52 to 112.60 ms. This is a useful operating point, but does not establish superiority across computational budgets.

The geometric analysis provides limited assurance about pose accuracy. Lemma 1 bounds an image-space residual by a quantity depending on triangle size; it does not bound the resulting pose error or establish convergence of refinement. Figure 9 also shows residual approximation error with noiseless measurements. The empirical results justify the method as a practical hypothesis generator, but broad claims that ENM makes scene dependence negligible remain insufficiently established.

A secondary reporting concern appears in Table 6: the Cambridge results for 4p3v(M)+R+F and 4p3v(M)+R+F+ENM exactly repeat the corresponding affine-solver rows, including runtimes. These apparent duplicates reduce confidence in those particular ablation entries, although they do not undermine the independent main-table evidence.
